To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the political context in which TARA and council collaborate is a key factor in the development and maintenance of collaborative advantage.

The institutional environment in which TARA and council collaborate has been shaped by the political context of the national environment, the political environment of the local authority and the local political context of the TARA and council.
the political environment in which mandated TARA and local authority collaboration is embedded is a major determinant of how collaboration is perceived and enacted.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the institutional environment shapes the political environment and in turn how the political environment impacts on the way that mandated TARA and councils collaborate.
how institutional pressure and power impact on the achievement of collaborative outcomes.
understanding the impact of institutional forces and power on mandated TARA/council collaboration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the national political environment, which includes legislation and traditions and customs, is the main institutional force that affects mandated TARA and Council collaboration.

the rhetoric of collaboration between TARA and council is not reflected in the reality of collaboration and that the reality is that the institutional pressure and power of the political environment has a negative impact on the ability of TARA and council to collaborate.
mandated collaboration between TARA and council is a political tool used to control the TARA sector and that TARA have been marginalized in the collaborative process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the national government's policy and legislation on TARA and council collaborative working is a major institutional force that has had a significant influence on the development of mandated TARA and councils collaboration in the UK and in particular on how mandated TARA and Council collaboration has developed in the London Borough of Tower Hamlets (LBTH).
we have shown that the national political environment is important in shaping the nature of the relationship between TARA and council.
we have been able to show that there are a number of factors that have influenced mandated TARA and Council collaboration.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the current policy and legislation that mandates collaboration is not effective and that there is a need for a new policy that recognizes the need for collaboration to be voluntary and that the current policy is not working and needs to be changed.
the institutional environment in which TARA and council collaborate is not a static environment.
the current institutional environment in which mandated TARA and councils collaborate is not one that supports collaborative advantage.
